# TwoProd on values of the program

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `two_prod_entry` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $p + e$ of $a b$:

$$p + e \approx a b.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `two_prod(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | `ProductAndError<T>` | `constexpr`, through Dekker's product ([`two_prod_dekker`](two_prod_dekker.md)) in constant evaluation; not a constant expression on finite operands on which an operation of Dekker's product overflows (a program that needs one does not compile; the message names `two_prod_overflows_in_constant_evaluation`, or with GCC the operation): it is one when $\lvert a\rvert, \lvert b\rvert \le 2^{996}$ and $\lvert ab\rvert \le 2^{1023}$ ($2^{115}$ and $2^{127}$ for `float`), a sufficient condition, not an exact one; where it is one, the same values when the product is exact, each its own error term below the threshold; rounds; `r.product` is $p$ and `r.error` is $e$; the operands are guarded, as factors of a fused operation ([rule R3](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)) |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $p = \mathrm{RN}(a b)$.
- $\lvert p + e - a b\rvert \le \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$.
- $p + e = a b$ exactly, when $a b = 0$ or $\lvert a b\rvert \ge \eta/(2u^2)$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $2^{-1075} \approx 2.4703 \times 10^{-324}$ | $2^{-150} \approx 7.0065 \times 10^{-46}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0.0`, `0x1p-1074` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-149f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0.0`, `0x1p-1074` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-149f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `two_prod_entry_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/EntryKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/EntryKernels.v), against `two_prod_entry_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions two_prod_entry_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition two_prod_entry_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let '(p, e) := two_prod_entry emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec p /\
  fmt emin prec e /\
  p = RN emin prec (a * b) /\
  Rabs ((p + e) - (a * b)) <= (1 / 2) * eta emin /\
  (((a * b) = 0 \/ bpow radix2 (2 * prec - 1) * eta emin <= Rabs (a * b)) -> (p + e) = (a * b)).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `two_prod_entry_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** two_prod on its guarded operands (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/two_prod_entry.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/two_prod_entry.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_prod`](two_prod.md).

```
# two_prod for the public building block kairn::two_prod (milestone2.md, "Building blocks on T"):
# both operands pass through guard, then two_prod (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation:
# architecture.md). two_prod only multiplies a and b, which R3 alone does not guard; but a compiler
# that sees one of them to be 1 rewrites fms(a, 1, p) as a - p and fuses a product a = x y of the
# program into it, so that the error term is that of the exact product (Apple clang 21 under
# -ffp-contract=fast, measured). After the guards each is a number of the format. Its claims are
# those of two_prod: the guard is the identity on numbers of the format. Not claimed: the sign of a
# zero error term, which the guard of a negative zero can change. In constant evaluation the variant
# of two_prod, Dekker's product, on the operands as they are: constant evaluation fuses nothing.

ga     = guard(a)
gb     = guard(b)
(p, e) = two_prod(ga, gb)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#two_prod_entry)).

| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 98 321 652 | 0 | 1 | 0 (exact) | yes |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
